react.question: Write a counterReducer(state, action) function for use with useReducer. It should handle { type: 'increment' }, { type: 'decrement' }, and { type: 'reset' }, and return the same state object unchanged for any other action type.
Write a debounce(fn, delay) function. The returned function should only call fn once, after `delay` ms have passed since the LAST time it was invoked (calling it repeatedly resets the timer).

testCases.label: only fires once after rapid repeated calls
testCases.check: return new Promise((resolve) => { let calls = 0; const d = debounce(() => { calls++ }, 40); d(); d(); d(); setTimeout(() => resolve(calls === 1), 120) })

testCases.label: fires again on a later, separate call
testCases.check: return new Promise((resolve) => { let calls = 0; const d = debounce(() => { calls++ }, 30); d(); setTimeout(() => { d(); setTimeout(() => resolve(calls === 2), 60) }, 80) })

react.question: Write a deepMerge(a, b) function that deeply merges two plain objects, with values from b overriding values from a at every nested level. Arrays and non-object values in b simply replace the value in a.

testCases.label: merges nested objects
testCases.check: const r = deepMerge({a:{x:1}}, {a:{y:2}}); return r.a.x === 1 && r.a.y === 2

testCases.label: arrays are replaced, not merged
testCases.check: const r = deepMerge({list:[1,2]}, {list:[3]}); return JSON.stringify(r.list) === JSON.stringify([3])

react.question: Write a TodoList component that accepts an items prop (a list of objects with text and done properties). TodoList also accepts an onItemClick function prop, which should be called when a user clicks an item in the list — but only if that item is not marked as done. If the item IS done, onItemClick should not be called, and the click event should not propagate to the list's own onClick handler.

testCases.label: Clicking a not-done item triggers onItemClick with that item
testCases.check: const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')); const items = [{text:'Buy milk', done:false},{text:'Walk dog', done:true}]; let clicked = null; root.render(React.createElement(TodoList, { items, onListClick: () => {}, onItemClick: (item) => { clicked = item } })); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20)); document.querySelectorAll('#root li')[0].dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20)); const pass = clicked && clicked.text === 'Buy milk'; root.unmount(); document.getElementById('root').innerHTML = ''; return pass

testCases.label: Clicking a done item does not trigger onItemClick or a parent click
testCases.check: const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')); const items = [{text:'Buy milk', done:false},{text:'Walk dog', done:true}]; let clicked = null; let listClicked = false; root.render(React.createElement(TodoList, { items, onListClick: () => { listClicked = true }, onItemClick: (item) => { clicked = item } })); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20)); document.querySelectorAll('#root li')[1].dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20)); const pass = clicked === null && listClicked === false; root.unmount(); document.getElementById('root').innerHTML = ''; return pass
